why: Source: two baseline minutes-per-cake figures, then for each of four options a step-chart gridline reading and a minutes-per-unit calculation, then a comparison against the baseline (about 11 steps); question: the identical structure with services and watchmakers (about 11 steps), including the same trap of crossing a step threshold.

Source: pick the right line and the two removed costs while ignoring the distractor wage, sum, divide by the translator wage, then pick the largest option that still pays (4 steps); question: the same four steps on the road range with the $27 wage as the distractor.

Source: take the complement of the machine-sorted share for each period, multiply each by its volume, then subtract (5 steps); question: the same complement, two multiplications and a difference (5 steps).

Source: five differences turned into percentage falls from labelled bars, then a ranking (6 steps, fewer using the common first entry); question: the same five percentage falls and a ranking with the same common-first-entry shortcut (6 steps).

Source: four statements to check, a share of today's total, two five-year growth rates, a ten-year projection against a combined total, and compound annual rates over 3 and 5 years (about 9 steps); question: the same four statement types on the same three-series line chart (about 9 steps).

Source: read two cumulative bars off gridlines, take the difference (the cumulative-height trap), multiply by the emerging-market total (3 to 4 steps); question: the same two gridline readings, difference and multiplication by the developing-market total (3 to 4 steps), with the global $196bn as an extra distractor that adds no step.

Source: one count-weighted comparison (sum the 1-ratings shares per group and weight by sample size) plus three share-only checks, a 3-and-above share comparison, a 3-and-above check across four criteria and a 1-or-2 comparison (about 10 steps); question: the same four checks, but the 3-and-above comparison for one criterion is also count-weighted, which adds one weighting step (about 11 steps).

Source: bottles per order, a threshold check, two litre-to-unit price conversions, two order values and an average (7 steps); question: the same seven steps, though the 1L conversion is trivial, so at most one step lighter.

Source: read five weekday values off gridlines (one kind of reading), sum, divide by 5 rather than 7 (the trap) (3 steps); question: the same gridline reading, sum and divide by 5 rather than 7 (3 steps).
Source: bottles per order, a threshold check, two per-litre to per-tube conversions, two order values and an average (7 steps); question: the same seven steps with 250mL and 400mL bottles.
